usage: wsp activity [<thread>] [--computer <computer>] [--wide]
  this computer's processes, or a box's, as Settings > Activity lists them:
  wsp's own, then each thread heaviest first with what it started, then what has
  no thread, each with its kind, ports, memory and CPU; a thread named shows its
  own alone, on this computer or the box it runs on

  --computer    the computer to read: this one, which is the default, or a box
                wsp computers lists
  --wide        each process's pid and whole command line, the run script and
                input pump of a turn on rows of their own, nothing cut to the
                terminal's width
  --json        print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                everything else on stderr
  --state       the state file the host serves
  --host        run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp activity end <pid> --started <ms> [--computer <computer>]
  ends one process on this computer and everything under it, by the pid and the
  start wsp activity --json listed: TERM, then KILL after 2 s; refuses a process
  wsp did not start, an agent, which wsp stop ends, and a pid that names another
  process now

  --started     the process's start as wsp activity --json lists it, startedAt
                in epoch milliseconds; a pid that started otherwise is refused
  --computer    the computer the process runs on, which must be this one; a
                box's go with its thread's settle and --processes stop
  --json        print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                everything else on stderr
  --state       the state file the host serves
  --host        run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp conversations [<project>] [--agent <id>]
  the conversations Claude Code and Codex kept in the project's folder and its
  worktrees outside wsp, newest first, each with its id, last change, size,
  branch and title, and whether another app holds it open; wsp run --resume <id>
  opens a thread on one

  --agent    one agent's conversations alone, by its catalog id; every agent's
             without it
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell
